title: Variable registry entry
description: Central registry of every flag/counter/text id used anywhere. The validator checks all references against this. Items are NOT variables — they have their own registry (item.schema.json, data/items.json) so they can carry a player-facing name and description.

name.description: Player-facing display name, e.g. "Rusted Key" for an item. Optional: `description` stays the authoring-facing note. Tools fall back to `description`, then the raw id.

kind.description: 'text' is a string-substitution slot, not a gate — text variables are never readable by a Condition. They are written by set_text and interpolated into player-facing strings as {var_id}.

default.description: boolean for flag, integer for counter, string for text. A text variable with no default renders its raw {placeholder} until a set_text runs.

writtenBy.description: Who writes this variable. 'data' (the default) means an authored effect writes it, and the hygiene passes expect to find one. 'engine' means the host writes it at runtime — free-text the player typed, or state the game computes — so 'never written' and 'read but never set' are expected and suppressed. Parlance has no input-capture concept; this is how data declares that boundary instead of faking a literal set_text.
